A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same research despite the changed title. Their methods, experiments, equations and figures can be matched reliably. v1 ends with references; v4 additionally contains Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Tables 1–2 and empirical analyses of token distributions, hidden states, reasoning traces and sampling behavior.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds MATH500 Pass@k experiments using four Qwen2.5 base-model sizes in Section 6.2 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The Dirichlet and Gumbel-Softmax decoding procedures remain unchanged; 'Stochastic Soft Thinking' largely renames the existing approach. Section 6.1 adds a proposed RL adaptation using continuous-density policy ratios in a clipped policy-gradient objective, but explicitly leaves full RL integration to future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight benchmarks across mathematics, knowledge Q&A and code generation. v4 corrects the earlier 'seven' count and describes existing datasets in Appendix A. The new exploration experiment reuses MATH500 rather than adding a task or domain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical comparator membership: greedy and sampled token decoding, vanilla soft thinking, and the two randomized variants in their respective comparisons. Figure 6 reuses discrete token thinking as the comparator. Newly discussed RL methods and CoLaR are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 introduces a substantial new evaluation protocol: MATH500 Pass@k for k = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 using Qwen2.5 base models of 0.5B, 1.5B, 3B and 7B parameters. The original three-model benchmark settings, decoding parameters and Average@32/Pass@1 reporting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds an exploration and test-time-scaling analysis across sampling budgets and model sizes, supporting a new central comparative claim. Most original behavioral and sampler analyses remain, but the separate top-1/top-2 token-probability diagnostics in v1 Figure 3(b–c) are removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: Average@32 reporting is retained, and shaded bands already appeared in v1's logit-lens analysis. v4 introduces no stated seed, repeated-run, confidence-level or significance-testing procedure. The new Pass@k attempt budgets concern evaluation design, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Every result row in Tables 1–2 is unchanged. New Figure 6 reports higher soft-thinking Pass@k across the four smaller Qwen2.5 models and tested budgets; these are additional settings, not improvements to the original table results. The logit-lens curves and bands also change while retaining the top-1-dominance trend.

T1.justification: Section 6.1 adds a mathematical RL formulation, including a purported Gumbel-Softmax density and continuous-token policy ratio. Existing definitions and Theorem 1 remain, while v1's explicit linear-mixture argument in Section 4.2 is removed. As printed, new Equation 9 lacks the inverse-power normalization factor and is not a normalizable density.

C1.justification: v4 elevates stronger exploration and test-time scaling relative to discrete CoT into an explicit abstract and introduction contribution, beyond v1's mechanistic diagnosis and benchmark-performance claims. The conclusion also weakens the description of Gumbel-Softmax from 'optimal' to 'ideal'; the general aspiration toward RL already existed in v1.

C2.justification: The new limitations section proposes architectural and next-token-training explanations for single-path behavior, discusses forgetting and base-model constraints, and questions whether RL alone can produce parallel reasoning. v4 also removes v1's speculative interpretation of QwQ results as possible overfitting and explicitly distinguishes exploration evidence from unperformed RL integration.

D1.justification: New Appendix A documents existing datasets' composition and sizes, including 30 problems per AIME edition, 40 AMC problems and 198 GPQA-Diamond questions. These are additional disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to test sets. Existing implementation and hyperparameter-search information is largely retained.

R1.justification: v4 substantially extends positioning toward RL for latent reasoning and exploration, discussing PPO, GRPO, REINFORCE++, CoLaR and Pass@k/capability-boundary literature. It also adds the superposition perspective of Zhu et al. These additions broaden the argument beyond the largely continuous-CoT positioning of v1.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around single-threaded reasoning and Stochastic Soft Thinking, with an explicit contribution list. Behavioral and theoretical explanations are condensed, and new RL, limitations and appendix sections reorganize the narrative beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 3–5 are reorganized into v4 Figure 3, combining retained entropy, logit-lens and prefix-similarity plots while dropping two probability panels. The prefix-length axis becomes logarithmic, plot styling changes, and a new four-panel Pass@k figure is added. The main tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful exploration evidence, dataset documentation and substantive scope discussion while preserving the original benchmark results and moderating the optimality claim. However, its new RL foundation relies on Equation 9, which is non-normalizable as printed and therefore does not justify Equation 10's policy ratio. The empirical and explanatory gains coexist with this material new theoretical defect, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
